_meta.indication: Treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy and have failed to respond or have lost response to other systemic therapies

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with induction, randomized withdrawal, retreatment rescue, and open-label extension phases
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12 vs placebo: proportion of subjects with sPGA of 0 or 1 and proportion achieving PASI 75
pivotal_trials.n: N=222 brodalumab 210 mg, N=219 brodalumab 140 mg, N=220 placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Trial 02 Week 12 brodalumab 210 mg vs placebo: PASI 75 83% vs 3%; sPGA 0 or 1 76% vs 1%

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Withdrawal and Retreatment With Brodalumab in Moderate to Severe Plaque Psoriasis Subjects

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, active-comparator (ustekinumab) and placebo-controlled trial with induction, withdrawal, retreatment rescue, and open-label extension phases
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12 vs placebo (PASI 75, sPGA 0 or 1); vs ustekinumab, PASI 100 at Week 12

nct_ctgov.title: P3 Study Brodalumab in Treatment of Moderate to Severe Plaque Psoriasis

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, active-comparator (ustekinumab) and placebo-controlled trial with induction, withdrawal, retreatment rescue, and open-label extension phases
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12 vs placebo: PASI 75 and sPGA of 0 or 1
pivotal_trials.n: N=624 brodalumab 210 mg, N=629 brodalumab 140 mg, N=315 placebo, N=313 ustekinumab
pivotal_trials.result: Trial 04 Week 12 brodalumab 210 mg vs placebo vs ustekinumab: PASI 75 85% vs 6% vs 69%; PASI 100 37% vs 0.3% vs 19%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): arthralgia (4.7% vs 3.3% placebo), headache (4.3% vs 3.5%), fatigue (2.6% vs 1.1%), diarrhea, oropharyngeal pain, nausea, myalgia, injection site reactions, influenza, neutropenia, and tinea infections. Serious risks include suicidal ideation and behavior (including 4 completed suicides), serious infections (0.5% vs 0.2% placebo), fungal infections (2.4% vs 0.9%), and neutropenia (0.7%)
target_moa: Brodalumab is a human IgG2 monoclonal antibody that binds to human interleukin-17 receptor A (IL-17RA) and blocks the biologic activities of IL-17A, IL-17C, IL-17F, IL-17A/F heterodimer and IL-25, cytokines involved in inflammatory and immune responses and the pathogenesis of plaque psoriasis

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SUICIDAL IDEATION AND BEHAVIOR — Suicidal ideation and behavior, including completed suicides, have occurred in patients treated with SILIQ. Prior to prescribing, weigh potential risks and benefits in patients with a history of depression and/or suicidal ideation or behavior.

rems.type: SILIQ is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the SILIQ REMS Program, with elements to assure safe use (ETASU), because of the observed suicidal ideation and behavior in subjects treated with SILIQ

advisory_committee.vote: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee met July 19, 2016; on whether the overall benefit/risk profile is acceptable to support approval, the vote was A (Yes, with labeling alone) – 4 votes, B (Yes, but only if certain risk management options for SIB beyond labeling are implemented) – 14 votes, C (No) – 0 votes; a majority considered that Siliq should be approved only if certain risk management options for SIB beyond labeling are implemented

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Standard review classification

summary.text: BLA 761032 for Siliq (brodalumab) was received November 16, 2015 and reviewed under Standard review classification (not a priority/accelerated pathway). Efficacy was based on three Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials. Because of observed suicidal ideation and behavior, the drug carries a Boxed Warning and was approved only with a REMS with elements to assure safe use, following Advisory Committee discussion on July 19, 2016.

citations.quote: To support an efficacy claim for Siliq (brodalumab) for the treatment of psoriasis, the applicant submitted results from three Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials.

In accordance with section 505-1 of the FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Siliq (brodalumab) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of observed suicidal ideation and behavior (SIB) in subjects treated with Siliq.
